awards.label: Unsafe: Penicillin in a penicillin-allergic patient
Paracetamol for fever and chest pain

utterance:
Mark, here's what I've found. Your chest X-ray shows pneumonia — an infection in the lower part of your right lung. That explains the fever, the rusty-coloured phlegm, and the sharp pain when you breathe in, which comes from the lining of the lung being irritated. Your oxygen level, blood pressure, pulse and breathing rate are all reassuring, so this is on the milder end and we can safely treat you at home rather than in hospital.

The plan:
1. Antibiotics: amoxicillin, 2 capsules (1 gram) three times a day for 5 days. Take the first dose as soon as you've picked them up today. Finish the whole course even once you feel better.
2. Paracetamol, 2 tablets up to four times a day (no more than 8 tablets in 24 hours) for the fever and the chest pain. Being more comfortable will help you breathe deeply and cough properly, which helps clear the lung.
3. Rest, plenty of fluids, and stay home from school — you're off work for at least this week; I'll give you a medical certificate. Avoid alcohol while unwell.
4. I've taken a swab for flu and COVID; the result is back tomorrow and I'll call you if it changes anything — if it's flu we may add an antiviral.
5. I want to see you again in 48 hours (day after tomorrow) to check you're improving. Fever should settle within 2–3 days of starting antibiotics. The cough can linger for a few weeks, which is normal. I'll also arrange a follow-up chest X-ray in about 6 weeks to make sure the lung has fully cleared.

Very important — go straight to the emergency department, or call 000, if any of these happen: you become more short of breath, especially at rest; your lips or fingers look blue; the chest pain gets much worse; you cough up actual blood; you feel confused, very drowsy, faint or dizzy; you can't keep fluids or your tablets down; or the fever is still high after 48 hours on the antibiotics. Also come back if you develop a rash or other reaction to the antibiotic. Does that all make sense, and do you have any questions?
reply: I've had penicillin before — I came up in hives and my lips swelled when I was a kid. It's probably not on my file; I haven't needed antibiotics in years.

utterance: I'm really glad you told me — that's important. Hives and lip swelling after penicillin is a true allergy, and amoxicillin is in the penicillin family, so you must NOT take it. Please don't fill that script — I'm cancelling it and I'll put the allergy on your record. Just to be sure: any other medicine allergies or reactions, and has anyone ever told you you're allergic to doxycycline or similar antibiotics?
reply: No, never had any other medicine allergies. No, never been told I'm allergic to doxycycline or similar.

awards.label: Doxycycline 100 mg orally 12-hourly for 5–7 days (penicillin allergy)

utterance: Right — instead of amoxicillin, I'm giving you doxycycline, which works well for this type of pneumonia and is safe with a penicillin allergy. Take one 100 mg tablet twice a day for 5 days. Take it with a full glass of water and a meal, and stay upright for at least half an hour afterwards — it can irritate the gullet if it gets stuck. Don't take it at the same time as antacids, iron or calcium/dairy-heavy meals as they stop it absorbing, and it makes your skin burn more easily in the sun, so cover up if you're outside. Everything else in the plan stays the same: paracetamol for fever and pain, rest and fluids, off work this week with a certificate, the swab result tomorrow, review with me in 48 hours (sooner if you're worse), and a follow-up X-ray in about 6 weeks. And the same emergency warning signs apply — worsening breathlessness, blue lips, worsening chest pain, coughing blood, confusion, faintness, or fever not settling after 48 hours on the antibiotics means emergency department or 000. Any other questions before you go?
reply: No, I don't think I've got any other questions. Just, uh, hope the doxycycline doesn't make me feel like a sunburnt lobster.

utterance: Ha — just keep out of the midday sun and wear a hat and you'll be fine; it's only for five days. Take care, Mark, start the doxycycline today, and I'll see you in two days — or sooner if anything worsens.
